ready_paragraphs.text: Writing reaches cinema through more than one kind of credit. In Maa, Gopal Chhotray and Biswajit Das share the dialogue credit, while Nitai Palit is credited with screenplay and direction. In Matira Manisha, Kalindi Charan Panigrahi supplies the literary story and Mrinal Sen’s filmography credits Sen with the screenplay. Naming those separate acts makes the collaboration more visible.

The route can also turn towards listening. Gopal Chhotray adapted Fakir Mohan Senapati’s Patent Medicine as Srimati Samarjani, catalogued by Odia Bibhaba as an opera. This belongs beside a cinema history as another transformation of literary voice, rather than as a film adaptation.

budget_limits: Each new source200derived words maximum across articles/book/notes; retained sources already shared with other chapters, so keep additions short and count globally. No copyrighted source passages or songs quoted. No full-book or film viewing asserted.
